spec.full_target: For every nonnegative integer n and every nonempty compact E⊆ℝ^n, with I=[0,1] and E×I given the metric induced from concatenated Euclidean coordinates in ℝ^(n+1), prove dim_H(E×I)=dim_H(E)+1.

calculations: The squared concatenated Euclidean product distance is the sum of the squared factor distances. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz; diam(U×J)≤√(diam(U)^2+diam(J)^2). Subdivide [0,1] into ≤1/r+1 intervals of length ≤r for 0<r≤1.

primitives.meaning: The n-dimensional real inner-product space, including the singleton ℝ^0.
The critical exponent of Hausdorff measures, with dim_H(∅)=0.

propositions.statement: For a set s in a Borel extended metric space and d∈ℝ≥0, if d<dim_H(s), then its d-dimensional Hausdorff measure is infinite.

source.statement: For a set s in a Borel extended metric space and d∈ℝ≥0, if d<dim_H(s), then its d-dimensional Hausdorff measure is infinite.

propositions.statement: For a countable family of nonnegative measurable ENNReal functions, the integral of their pointwise sum equals the sum of their integrals.

argument.text: Put D=dim_H(E), F=E×I. Compactness implies boundedness; covers of a bounded Euclidean box by O(k^n) cubes of diameter O(1/k) give H^q(E)=0 for q>n, hence D<∞. For q>D, M001 implies H^q(E)=0. At each δ≤1 choose a cover by positive-diameter r_j≤δ with arbitrarily small Σr_j^q, replacing singleton members by tiny balls of arbitrarily small total added q-cost. Cover I for each j by ≤1/r_j+1 intervals of length ≤r_j. The products cover F, have diameter ≤√2r_j, and total (q+1)-cost ≤2(√2)^(q+1)Σr_j^q. Let costs and then δ tend to zero: H^(q+1)(F)=0, so dim_H(F)≤D+1.

When D>0, fix 0<s<D. By M001, H^s(E)=∞, so the scale contents c_s(E,δ) tend to infinity as δ decreases to zero, directly by the definition of Hausdorff measure as the limit of these contents. Consider any countable cover V_i of F with ρ_i=diam(V_i)≤δ≤1; let A_i,B_i be coordinate projections, with diameters ≤ρ_i. Enclose B_i in an open interval J_i of length ≤ρ_i+η_i, where η_i>0 and Ση_iρ_i^s<ε. For every t∈I, the A_i with t∈J_i cover E, because each (x,t) lies in some V_i and B_i⊆J_i. Thus c_s(E,δ)≤Σ1_{J_i}(t)ρ_i^s pointwise. The indicators are measurable and nonnegative, and M002 applies the integral-of-sum identity; integration over I yields c_s(E,δ)≤Σ|J_i∩I|ρ_i^s≤Σρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Zero-diameter terms vanish since s>0. Let ε→0 and take the infimum over product covers to get c_s(E,δ)≤c_(s+1)(F,δ); hence H^(s+1)(F)=∞ and dim_H(F)≥s+1. This holds for all 0<s<D, so dim_H(F)≥D+1.

When D=0, choose x₀∈E by H001. The projection π:F→I is 1-Lipschitz and onto in the displayed concatenated Euclidean metric. Any countable cover of I by sets of diameter ≤δ has sum of diameters at least 1, since the interval length is 1 and each set is contained in an interval of the same diameter (or arbitrarily slightly larger). Thus H^1(I)>0 and dim_H(I)≥1. Its subdivision into intervals gives H^q(I)=0 for every q>1, hence dim_H(I)≤1. The elementary Lipschitz-cover estimate dim_H(π(F))≤dim_H(F) follows by mapping each cover member and using diameter nonincrease. Therefore dim_H(F)≥1=D+1. This includes n=0. Combining with the upper bound proves equality.

hypothesis_checks: Apply to E in Euclidean Borel space with q>D.
Apply to E in Euclidean Borel space with 0<s<D.
Apply counting measure on I to nonnegative measurable functions ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}; each J_i is open.
